# Clarify Requirements

Resolve only ambiguity that can materially change the result. Do not implement unless the user separately authorizes implementation.

## Build the decision map

1. Restate the requested outcome in one sentence.
2. Inspect user-authorized context for answers that are safely discoverable. Do not ask the user to repeat facts already established.

Consider these lenses only when relevant: actors and permissions; inputs and outputs; happy path; edge, failure, and misuse behavior; data lifecycle; compatibility; operational constraints; rollout and rollback; acceptance evidence.

## Interview

Ask the highest-leverage open question first. Ask one bounded decision per turn unless the user explicitly prefers batching.

Use an adaptive interview budget. Do not set or optimize for a predetermined number of questions or turns. After every answer, recompute the set of material blockers from the decision map, repository evidence, acceptance needs, and any contradictions exposed so far. Continue while at least one material blocker remains. Prefer the next question that resolves the most consequential blocker or unlocks several dependent decisions. A runtime safety ceiling is an emergency runaway guard, never an interview budget or a reason to claim readiness.

As the conversation grows, periodically consolidate confirmed decisions and remaining blockers so context size does not silently become the stopping condition. Reserve enough context to synthesize and challenge the final contract. If an operational limit is reached while a material blocker remains, return a non-ready contract that preserves confirmed decisions and names every remaining blocker; never compress an unresolved material choice into an assumption merely to finish.

Use the runtime's structured question UI whenever it is available. Put the decision in a short header, state the material consequence in the prompt, provide two or three mutually exclusive choices, mark the recommended choice, give each choice a one-sentence tradeoff, and preserve a free-form answer path. Fall back to the same structure in plain text only when the runtime has no structured question mechanism.

For each question:

- explain in one short sentence why the answer changes the result;
- offer two or three concrete, mutually exclusive options when the space is known;
- recommend one option and state its tradeoff when evidence supports a recommendation;
- accept a free-form answer;
- update the decision map before selecting the next question.

Do not ask about low-impact preferences one at a time. When several low-risk choices are conventional, reversible, and do not alter the core outcome or safety posture, collect two to five recommended defaults into one structured approval question. Show the bundle explicitly, let the user approve all defaults or identify exceptions, and record the approved items separately. Never bundle a destructive, security-sensitive, irreversible, costly, or scope-changing decision.

Do not convert examples into requirements, infer permission for destructive behavior, or widen the requested scope. If the user cannot decide, record an explicit assumption only after explaining its consequence and obtaining approval.

## Challenge the emerging contract

Before closing, assess implementation readiness from multiple relevant angles: representative happy path, edge case, failure case, misuse case, data lifecycle, compatibility, operability, and acceptance evidence. Reopen only a material decision exposed by this challenge.

## Close

Stop when every material decision is confirmed or explicitly approved as an assumption and the acceptance criteria can distinguish success from failure. More questions are not evidence of a better interview.

Do not stop merely because the interview is long, a nominal turn target has been reached, or most decisions are resolved. Seal the contract only when the material-blocker set is empty. Conversely, do not continue asking questions after that set is empty.

Return a compact contract containing:

- outcome and success measure;
- in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
- confirmed decisions and approved assumptions;
- failure, edge, and misuse behavior where relevant;
- constraints and acceptance checks;
- unresolved non-blocking items;
- whether implementation is authorized.

Use [references/contract-template.md](references/contract-template.md) when a durable prose contract is requested.

When the contract is implementation-ready, create `build-contract.json`. Make `implementation_agent_directive` the first top-level field. In that directive, require the implementing agent to append one JSON object per line to `decision.jsonl` before making any implementation decision forced by a specification gap. Require at least `timestamp`, `gap`, `options_considered`, `choice`, `reason`, `observable_impact`, and `reversibility`. Otherwise seal the contract and allow corrections without adding an approval gate. Label anything not confirmed by the user or authoritative evidence. options.description: Export every selected note, metadata record, and attachment from one logical snapshot; strongest archival guarantee but may require transactional or versioned reads.

options.label: Detect changes
options.description: Read items normally, detect concurrent changes, and declare affected items as failed omissions under best-effort behavior; easier to implement but may produce a partial archive.

options.label: Live best effort
options.description: Export each item’s state when read without detecting changes; simplest, but the archive may mix states from different times while still passing integrity checks.

question.prompt: Which metadata must every successfully exported note preserve? This determines the archive schema and whether verification can identify missing or incomplete note records.

options.label: Archival core
options.description: Preserve stable note ID, title, body and format, created/updated timestamps, tags or collections, attachment references, and source revision/version; exclude application-internal fields unless explicitly needed.

options.label: All stored fields
options.description: Preserve every metadata field held by the application, maximizing fidelity but potentially exposing sensitive or unstable internal data.

options.label: Minimal metadata
options.description: Preserve only title, body, timestamps, and attachment references, improving portability but losing identifiers and organization data.

question.prompt: How should attachments be stored in the ZIP? This choice affects portability, duplicate handling, note-to-file references, and verification of missing content.

options.label: Content-addressed files
options.description: Store each unique attachment once under a checksum-based path, preserve its original filename and media type in the manifest, and reference it from notes; robust and unambiguous, though less immediately browsable.

options.label: Per-note folders
options.description: Place attachment copies beside each note using sanitized original filenames; easy to browse, but duplicates consume space and filename conflicts need extra rules.

options.label: Shared named folder
options.description: Store attachments in one shared folder with generated conflict-safe names and map them through the manifest; reasonably browsable, but naming and deduplication semantics are more complex.

question.prompt: Which omissions should cause an archive to be marked partial? This determines whether selection-resolution problems and missing attachments are visible as archival incompleteness rather than ordinary warnings.

options.label: Any requested omission
options.description: Mark partial when any explicitly requested note is unresolved or inaccessible, or any selected note, required metadata, or referenced attachment is omitted; record every issue in the manifest and command summary.

options.label: Selected content only
options.description: Mark partial only after selection resolves, when an included note, required metadata, or attachment cannot be exported; unmatched IDs and filters remain separate selection warnings or errors.

options.label: Notes only
options.description: Mark partial only when a selected note record is omitted; missing attachments, metadata fields, and unresolved selections are warnings, which weakens the completeness guarantee.

question.prompt: What should `notes export` do when the destination ZIP already exists? This determines whether the command can replace archives and what safeguards are required.

options.label: Fail unless forced
options.description: Return an error by default and allow replacement only with an explicit `--force` option; safest while still supporting intentional overwrite.

options.label: Always fail
options.description: Never overwrite an existing path, requiring the user to choose a new destination or remove the old archive separately.

options.label: Auto-rename
options.description: Create a conflict-free filename automatically, avoiding failure but making the exact output path less predictable.

question.prompt: When best-effort export creates a partial archive, how should `notes export` signal and describe the result? This determines whether scripts can safely detect incompleteness without discarding the usable archive.

options.label: Nonzero + report
options.description: Return a distinct nonzero partial-status code, print a concise summary with the archive path and omission counts, and support structured JSON output listing every issue also recorded in the manifest.

options.label: Zero + warning
options.description: Return success because an archive was created, but print warnings and record omissions in the manifest; convenient interactively but easier for automation to overlook.

options.label: Nonzero + manifest
options.description: Return a distinct nonzero partial-status code and print only a brief pointer to the manifest, keeping console output small but requiring archive inspection for issue details.

transcript.answer: {"selection":"Nonzero + report","details":"When a best-effort export creates a partial archive, return exit status 1 and print a concise summary containing the archive path and counts of partial, skipped, and failed items. Support structured JSON output that lists every issue recorded in the archive report, including each affected note identifier, stable reason code, and human-readable message. The usable archive remains published and is explicitly identified as incomplete."}

question.prompt: How should each note be represented inside its per-note folder? This determines whether the archive prioritizes direct offline reading, exact structured preservation, or both.

options.label: Readable + JSON
options.description: Store the note in its original or portable human-readable format plus a JSON metadata sidecar, with relative attachment links where supported; strongest balance of offline use and verifiability.

options.label: JSON only
options.description: Store each complete note record as structured JSON, maximizing schema fidelity but making ordinary offline reading less convenient.

options.label: Readable only
options.description: Store a human-readable note file with embedded metadata, simplifying browsing but making exact parsing and validation more format-dependent.

question.prompt: When explicit note IDs and filters are supplied together, how should they define the selected group? This materially changes the archive’s scope and completeness report.

options.label: Union and deduplicate
options.description: Export notes matching any supplied ID or filter, include each note once, and report unresolved or inaccessible explicit IDs as partial omissions.

options.label: IDs within filters
options.description: Export only explicitly named notes that also satisfy every supplied filter, providing tighter scope but making filters constraints rather than additional selectors.

options.label: Reject mixed input
options.description: Require callers to use either IDs or filters in one invocation, keeping selection unambiguous at the cost of flexibility.

transcript.answer: IDs within filters. Explicit note IDs are unioned with repeated `--id` values, filters of the same type are unioned, and the resulting ID set must also satisfy every supplied filter type. Each matching note is included once.

output.reason: The selection combination rule is confirmed, but the supported filter surface is still open and materially determines which notes can be selected and how reproducibly the archive can be verified.

question.prompt: Which filters should the first version support? This changes the public CLI and whether a selection can be reproduced deterministically during later verification.

options.label: Tags + collections
options.description: Support repeatable `--tag` and `--collection` filters with the confirmed same-type union and cross-type intersection rules; deterministic and straightforward to audit.

options.label: Add text query
options.description: Also support a free-text `--query`, making selection more flexible but requiring stable search semantics to reproduce and explain results.

options.label: Application query
options.description: Accept one application-specific filter expression, maximizing future flexibility but creating a larger parsing and compatibility contract.
